Pearson and Spearman Rank correlation analysis
Gray Level Co-Occurrence Matrix (GLCM) Texture Analysis

National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS)
Application Areas: Automated Misinformation Detection and Public Media Literacy

Computational Geoscience and Unconventional Shale Characterization

Key Research Thinking Patterns: Explainable Regression-Based Trust Scoring: Integrating communication-based NLP dimensions with fine-tuned Large Language Models to quantify article trustworthiness, specifically utilizing RoBERTa to achieve superior correlation and lower MSE compared to BERT and DistilBERT baselines.

Composite Radiomic-Clinical Machine Learning: Combining volumetric imaging markers (ASPECTS/PC-ASPECTS) with clinical features and applying Recursive Feature Elimination to train SVM and Logistic Regression models for high-accuracy prediction of functional outcomes in stroke survivors.

Multi-Modal Image-Driven Property Prediction: Correlating Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) textural attributes, pore shape features, and deep learning embeddings (ResNet-50) with decision tree regression to estimate rock mechanical properties like Young's modulus without extensive laboratory testing.

Human-in-the-Loop Visual Analytics: Developing interactive tools that combine AI-powered geolocation prediction with passive-aggressive classifiers to enable real-time misinformation tracking and classification, validated through case studies of geo-tagged social media data.
Summary Description: David Ebert is a data scientist specializing in the intersection of Natural Language Processing, Medical Imaging, and Computational Geoscience. His research focuses on developing explainable AI (XAI) and machine learning frameworks to address societal challenges, including misinformation detection, clinical prognosis, and resource exploration. Key methodologies include fine-tuning Transformer architectures (RoBERTa) for trustworthiness scoring, integrating radiomic features with clinical data for stroke outcome prediction, and using SEM image analysis to predict rock mechanics. Ebert’s work emphasizes the translation of complex data into actionable insights through visual analytics and human-in-the-loop systems, contributing to advancements in public health informatics, national security, and energy engineering.
